cartridges.name: 9mm Luger (9x19mm Parabellum)
cartridges.notes: Headspaces on the case mouth: use a TAPER crimp only (no roll crimp); crimp just enough to remove bell. Cases rarely need trimming; published trim-to varies 0.749-0.750 in. Case is tapered, so a carbide die avoids lube. Bullet setback in semi-autos raises pressure sharply; verify neck tension and seat to the COAL in your data. +P is 38,500 psi (SAAMI) and needs +P data. Some 'Blazer' aluminum and steel cases are Berdan/non-reloadable; discard. Hornady HAP 125 gr is .356 in.

cartridges.name: .223 Remington (and 5.56x45mm NATO)
cartridges.typicalTwist: 1:12 (SAAMI .223 Rem); AR-15/5.56 barrels commonly 1:7 to 1:9. Heavy bullets (75-80+ gr) generally need 1:8 or faster (Sierra: 77 gr SMK requires 1:8 or faster)
cartridges.notes: 5.56 NATO uses the same external case dimensions but a longer freebore/leade and is loaded to higher pressure measured by a different method (NATO EPVAT, not directly comparable to SAAMI's 55,000 psi). Firing 5.56 loads in a .223-only chamber can over-pressure; .223 in a 5.56 chamber is fine. Load to .223 data unless your manual has specific 5.56 data and your chamber is 5.56/.223 Wylde. Military (e.g., Lake City) brass has crimped primer pockets that must be swaged/reamed and often slightly less capacity. For ARs many use harder-cup primers (CCI 450, CCI #41, Federal GM205MAVS) to reduce slam-fire/pierce risk. Mag length limits COAL to ~2.260 in for AR mags; long heavy bullets may need single-feeding. Trim when cases exceed 1.760.

cartridges.name: 7mm PRC (Precision Rifle Cartridge)
cartridges.notes: Belt-less magnum on a .532 in case head (same as the other PRCs/.300 RUM family), 30-degree shoulder, designed for long heavy bullets (175-195 gr) in a long action at 3.340 in max COAL; longer is possible if your magazine/throat allow. Large Rifle MAGNUM primers are recommended (Rifle Shooter/Hornady guidance: the large charges of slow magnum powder call for magnum ignition), e.g. Federal 215/215M, CCI 250, Winchester WLRM. Uses slow magnum powders. Gross water capacity of Hornady brass reported ~78-82 gr H2O depending on method. Trim-to is listed as 2.260 in by Rifle Shooter; check your manual. Brass is available from Hornady, Peterson, Nosler and Lapua (all large rifle primer pockets).
